title: CoreWeave sinks 17% as CEO calls market ‘irrational’ amid AI debt rout
source_used: Stocktwits on TradingView (citing Bloomberg News) / The Motley Fool
key_facts: CoreWeave shares fell by up to 17% during Wednesday's session (14 Oct 2026).
The company's unsecured bonds hit levels that show distress (Stocktwits).
A social media post showed the bond yield had hit 15% (Motley Fool).
CEO Mike Intrator said in a memo seen by Bloomberg that the market is acting irrationally.
Intrator said the deal backlog is large enough to more than support its debt obligations.
CoreWeave's market value stays above $36.5 billion (Stocktwits).
Nebius Group fell over 9% in sympathy (Motley Fool).
quote_evidence: Shares of CRWV plunged by up to 17% during Wednesday's session.
CoreWeave's deal backlog is large enough to more than support its debt obligations, Intrator said in a memo that was seen by Bloomberg News.
CoreWeave plummeted 15% after a social media post showed its bond yield had hit 15%, spooking investors concerned about rising borrowing costs.
why_it_matters_hint: CoreWeave leans on debt to buy chips and build data centres, so rising yields hit it hard.
